Field notes from Beirut on building bilingual Arabic-English websites, sharp brand positioning, and digital experiences that convert.

Guide 01 · Bilingual UX

Why Arabic-English websites break—and how to design them properly

Most bilingual websites treat Arabic as a translated afterthought: English fonts fall back to system Arial, margins invert awkwardly, and headlines lose their editorial rhythm. At Digits Studio, we design LTR and RTL in parallel—pairing high-contrast English serifs like Playfair Display with modern Arabic typefaces like Alexandria and IBM Plex Sans Arabic, using logical CSS properties so layouts mirror cleanly.

Guide 02 · Conversion

The 5-Second Test: Turning interest into a clear next step

When a visitor lands on your homepage, they ask three questions immediately: What do you do? Who is it for? What should I click next? Replacing vague slogans with a plain-English offer, pairing it with real proof, and keeping one unmistakable Signal-Yellow action pill above the fold consistently outperforms bloated agency templates.

Guide 03 · Brand Systems

Brand, Website, Marketing: One connected idea, brought to life

Hiring three separate freelancers for your logo, your website, and your social templates creates friction and inconsistent messaging. When positioning, visual identity, web engineering, and launch creative share the same design tokens and voice, your business looks established from day one.
